$comment: PTN translation dictionary — the terms every locale must render the same way.
Modelled on the Ubuntu Belarusian Translators' dictionary:
https://wiki.ubuntu.com/UbuntuBelarusianTranslators/Dictionary
Two uses, one source of truth:
* `term` is uploaded to DeepL as a glossary, so a machine translation lands
on the house word instead of a synonym of the day.
* every locale string whose English source contains one of `match` is
checked for that locale's `stem`, and the ones that drifted are reported.
`stem` is the inflection-proof prefix the check looks for, not a word:
Slavic and Finnic cases mean the surface form in a string rarely equals the
dictionary form. A stem may be a list when a locale has two legitimate roots.
`status`: confirmed = the word a human translator already used in this repo;
proposed = written for a language PTN has no native reviewer for yet — a
reviewer changes it here, then the affected strings are retranslated and rechecked.
`enforce`: glossary = uploaded to DeepL so the engine must use this word;
check = verified after translation only. Forcing a heavily inflected noun
through a glossary makes DeepL paste the dictionary form into a slot that
needed a different case (Latvian produced the non-word "atiejošajiem" that
way), so prose nouns are checked, and only labels and words the engine gets
outright wrong are forced.
`exceptions` lists keys where the English word appears in some other sense.
DeepL supports a glossary for every locale here except be (Belarusian), where
the dictionary is enforced by the check alone.
`doNotTranslate` is uploaded to DeepL verbatim. Most entries are proper
nouns; "LIVE" is there for layout, not language. It is a fixed-width mono
all-caps marker sharing a row with a truncated stop name, so every locale
renders the same four characters and the badge keeps a known size. The
title-case prose around it (route.live_prefix, route.may_miss) is still
translated normally — only the badge label is pinned.

stop.note: A transit stop — the place a vehicle calls at. Never the verb 'to stop', never 'station'.

departure.note: A scheduled departure from a stop, the noun the whole departures board is built on.

transfer.note: Changing from one vehicle to another mid-trip. Not a file transfer, not a money transfer.

route.note: A computed itinerary shown to the user. The drawn transit line is 'line', not 'route'.

trip.note: The user's journey end to end, across every leg. GTFS's own `trip` (one run of a service) is a different word in Slavic transit usage — рейс / рэйс — and the rt.* warnings and the trip sheet's status lines (trip.cancelled / removed / finished) use that sense.

walk.note: Travelling on foot as a leg of a trip.

schedule.note: The timetable a city publishes. 'Schedule view' is the map-free departures screen.

platform.note: A numbered boarding position inside a stop group.

line.note: A transit line (bus 10, tram 3). Never a line of text — that is 'row'.

settings.note: The settings screen and the word on its tab.

et.note: Estonian 'seaded' (settings) and 'seade' (device) share a stem, so the checker cannot tell them apart here — it is the common Android wording and worth the blind spot.

delay.note: A vehicle running late against its schedule.

cancelled.note: A trip the operator has cancelled. Rail wording, not 'deleted'.

bike share.note: The shared-bike layer (GBFS). One noun, the name people know it by locally.

bike.note: A bicycle — the vehicle, and the mobility profile. Belarusian uses ровар, not the Russian-influenced веласіпед: a reviewer's call, and the reason the be column reads the way it does.

device.note: The user's phone or computer — the thing routing runs on. Privacy copy leans on it.

offline.note: No network. The app is built to keep working here, so the word carries weight.

privacy.note: The privacy model and its levels. Swedish 'integritet' and Norwegian 'personvern' are the standard terms — a machine will otherwise reach for 'privatliv', which means private life.

hub.note: A stop flagged as an interchange.

arrival.note: Arriving at a stop or at the destination.

accessibility.note: Accessibility features — colour schemes, screen-reader support, mobility profiles.

micromap.note: PTN's own on-device basemap. A coined product word: translate it as a compound, do not borrow the English.

trolleybus.note: GTFS route_type 11. Vilnius and Gdynia both run them, so the word is load-bearing.

rail.note: GTFS route_type 2 — a train. Locale terms here follow each city's habit rather than a literal 'rail': ru/uk say электричка/електричка, be чыгунка.
